check-fds-conformity.mjs's bridge-freshness check reads theme.css from a hardcoded sibling path (../filigran-design-system relative to the product), so it only means anything when that sibling is actually at the pinned library commit. Check the sibling before believing either verdict: a STALE against a sibling that is behind the pin says nothing, and — the trap that cost this pilot three weeks — an OK against a sibling that happens to match a stale bridge says nothing either. The 2026-08-11 pass replaced an earlier version of this note which asserted the STALE was a false positive; it was not. theme.css was byte-identical at origin/main, at the pin and in the sibling checkout, and none of the three matched the hash recorded in the bridge: the bridge really had been generated from the 2026-07-16 theme.css and was 12 library commits behind. Verify by hashing, never by assuming. 2026-08-24 — no longer true: the regenerated script hashes the INSTALLED package and names that source in its verdict.

(a) The list select-all boxes (ListLines, DataTableHeaders) -- the library box is a bare 16px button where MUI's was a self-centring 42px control, so each slot now centres it explicitly; that offset was the reported header misalignment. (b) The form boxes, which drop FormControlLabel for the library's own `label` and move from onChange(event) to onCheckedChange(boolean); each of their three handlers had exactly one call site and was re-typed to a boolean rather than fed a synthetic event. The boxes rendered inside a library Combobox option row take `presentational`: a real control nested in an option is an axe nested-interactive failure that aria-hidden does not clear. ONE site is deliberately excepted -- FilterChipPopover's filter-value row. night-2 visual pass: the `Add filter` picker. It never HOLDS a value -- picking an option adds a filter and the field empties -- so `value` is a literal null and ONLY a keystroke may write the input: in single mode the library answers a pick with setInputValue(getOptionLabel(option), "select"), and accepting that programmatic write left the field reading "Label" after the filter was added, so filling the same text a second time fired no input event and never reopened the panel. The name rides on `placeholder` + aria-label under `labelPosition="none"`: the library renders labels ABOVE the control, and this one shares a flex row with an unlabelled search field. Covered by ListFilters.picker.test.tsx, which mirrors filters.pageModel's two-pass sequence.
